scope: Curated teaching synthesis; broad reference anatomy is distinct from study-specific parcels, streamlines and contact localization.

sources.title: Efficacy of transcranial magnetic stimulation targets for depression is related to intrinsic functional connectivity with the subgenual cingulate

sources.title: White matter pathways mediating dorsolateral prefrontal TMS therapy for depression

sources.title: Randomized sham-controlled trial of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation in treatment-resistant obsessive–compulsive disorder
sources.label: Mantovani 2010

sources.title: Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation–Induced Plasticity Improving Cognitive Control in Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder, Part I: Clinical and Neuroimaging Outcomes From a Randomized Trial
sources.label: Fitzsimmons 2025
sources.sample: 66 randomized; 64 began treatment; 61 clinical completers (19 DLPFC, 23 pre-SMA, 19 vertex); 54 fMRI completers (16, 20, 18)
sources.targeting: Left DLPFC or left pre-SMA, using task-fMRI peaks when available. All DLPFC targets were individualized; 74% of pre-SMA targets used the published fallback coordinate. Low-intensity vertex control.
sources.protocol: 16 sessions over 8 weeks, immediately before ERP; 10 Hz and 3,000 pulses in all arms. DLPFC/pre-SMA: 110% resting motor threshold; vertex: 60%.
sources.map_role: Compare left DLPFC and left pre-SMA targets, task networks, and vertex control.
sources.review_status: Supplied full text and relevant figures/tables reviewed; Round 3, 2026-10-01; 39-page supplement and resources workbook reviewed

lessons.title: From a cortical target to a mood network
lessons.question: Why stimulate the DLPFC?

edges.label: Functional anticorrelation
edges.description: Better outcomes were associated with more negative resting-state connectivity between the stimulated DLPFC site and sgACC. This relationship does not identify a direct fiber or establish a complete treatment mechanism.

edges.label: Frontostriatal context
edges.description: Reference corticostriatal fibers supply anatomical context. Healthy-volunteer TMS–PET supports a downstream caudate effect, not proof that this bundle mediates depression improvement.

steps.title: Start at the cortical target
steps.body: The coil is positioned over left DLPFC. “DLPFC” covers a broad cortical region; the precise stimulation site varies across targeting approaches.
steps.takeaway: The treatment entry point is cortical.
steps.note: Left middle-frontal parcels approximate DLPFC; no coil field is shown.

steps.title: Connect the target to sgACC
steps.body: Fox and Weigand linked antidepressant response to the functional relationship between the stimulation site and sgACC. More negative resting-state connectivity was associated with better response.
steps.takeaway: A useful targeting relationship is not the same thing as a direct tract.
steps.note: The dashed line is functional. Left-side sgACC is an orientation surface, not the reported seed location. No direct DLPFC–sgACC fiber is drawn.

steps.title: Keep the deep circuit in view
steps.body: Prefrontal stimulation can affect deeper structures. A TMS–PET experiment in healthy volunteers found a dopamine response in the ipsilateral caudate. The atlas’s corticostriatal tract gives this relationship anatomical context.
steps.takeaway: TMS has downstream effects beyond the cortex under the coil.
steps.note: The displayed tract is a whole reference bundle, not a patient’s stimulated fibers.

steps.title: Carry the right explanation into clinic
steps.body: DLPFC TMS is a cortical intervention with network effects. Functional targeting studies support the sgACC relationship, while the exact anatomical routes and causal mechanisms require additional evidence.
steps.takeaway: Say “network-informed targeting”; avoid “a direct wire to the depression center.”
steps.locator: Conclusions; interpretation of the cited studies
steps.note: No treatment strength, direction of electrical flow, or individual response is encoded.

quiz.question: Does the dashed DLPFC–sgACC connection represent a direct anatomical tract?
quiz.answer: No. It represents resting-state functional connectivity. The separate corticostriatal bundle shows structural context.

lessons.title: How might DLPFC stimulation reach sgACC?
lessons.question: Compare three proposed multistep routes

edges.label: Callosal crossing
edges.description: A proposed step in Seguin’s normative connectome model. Direction follows the modeled route; it is not observed electrical propagation. The 3D bundles are separately sourced reference anatomy.

edges.label: Cortical step
edges.description: A proposed step in Seguin’s normative connectome model. Direction follows the modeled route; it is not observed electrical propagation. The 3D bundles are separately sourced reference anatomy.

edges.label: Cingulum
edges.description: A proposed step in Seguin’s normative connectome model. Direction follows the modeled route; it is not observed electrical propagation. The 3D bundles are separately sourced reference anatomy.

edges.label: To left thalamus
edges.description: A proposed step in Seguin’s normative connectome model. Direction follows the modeled route; it is not observed electrical propagation. The 3D bundles are separately sourced reference anatomy.

edges.label: To medial cortex
edges.description: A proposed step in Seguin’s normative connectome model. Direction follows the modeled route; it is not observed electrical propagation. The 3D bundles are separately sourced reference anatomy.

edges.label: Later crossing
edges.description: A proposed step in Seguin’s normative connectome model. Direction follows the modeled route; it is not observed electrical propagation. The 3D bundles are separately sourced reference anatomy.

edges.label: To sgACC
edges.description: A proposed step in Seguin’s normative connectome model. Direction follows the modeled route; it is not observed electrical propagation. The 3D bundles are separately sourced reference anatomy.

edges.label: To right thalamus
edges.description: A proposed step in Seguin’s normative connectome model. Direction follows the modeled route; it is not observed electrical propagation. The 3D bundles are separately sourced reference anatomy.

edges.label: To medial cortex
edges.description: A proposed step in Seguin’s normative connectome model. Direction follows the modeled route; it is not observed electrical propagation. The 3D bundles are separately sourced reference anatomy.

steps.title: A route through cortex
steps.body: Seguin proposes left DLPFC → right dorsal superior frontal gyrus → right anterior cingulate cortex → right SGC. This three-step route crosses hemispheres through the corpus callosum and reaches SGC through the cingulum.
steps.takeaway: Several connections can link two regions without a direct DLPFC–sgACC tract.
steps.locator: Main text p. 1050; Figure 2g–h; Supplementary Figure S7
steps.note: The diagram follows the proposed route. Broad 3D regions and reference bundles do not reproduce its individual streamlines.

steps.title: The left-thalamus route
steps.body: Another route proceeds from left DLPFC to left thalamus, left medial superior frontal cortex, right medial superior frontal cortex and right SGC. The hemispheric crossing occurs after the left thalamic relay.
steps.takeaway: The thalamus supplies a possible intermediate relay.
steps.locator: Main text p. 1050; Figure 2h; Supplementary Figure S6
steps.note: The diagram follows the proposed route. Broad 3D regions and reference bundles do not reproduce its individual streamlines.

steps.title: The right-thalamus route
steps.body: Here the crossing occurs earlier: left DLPFC → right dorsal superior frontal cortex → right thalamus → right medial superior frontal cortex → right SGC. This is a different four-step alternative, not an additional segment of the left-thalamus route.
steps.takeaway: Keep alternative routes separate rather than joining them into one long tract.
steps.locator: Main text p. 1050; Figure 2h; Supplementary Figure S8
steps.note: The diagram follows the proposed route. Broad 3D regions and reference bundles do not reproduce its individual streamlines.

steps.title: What supports these routes?
steps.body: In two existing TMS cohorts (25 and 24 participants), fewer modeled hops were associated with greater symptom improvement. The supplied data reproduce the first cohort’s correlation (ρ≈−0.51). Two of four cohort/connectome combinations remained significant after correction across nine network measures.
steps.takeaway: These routes are testable anatomical hypotheses, not proven pathways of antidepressant action.
steps.locator: Figure 1c,g; Methods; Supplementary Figure S3; Source Data Figure 1, sheet 1C
steps.note: The diagram follows the proposed route. Broad 3D regions and reference bundles do not reproduce its individual streamlines.

quiz.question: Does “four hops” mean four millimeters or four directly observed synapses?
quiz.answer: Neither. A hop is one modeled connection between parcels in a normative graph. The selected route minimizes a weight-based cost; it is not a measured physical path length or a count of observed synapses.

lessons.title: A cortical entry point into OCD circuitry
lessons.question: Why target medial frontal cortex?

edges.label: Corticostriatal arm
edges.description: A selected arm of the circuit motivating the H7 protocol. The study tested a treatment protocol, not selective activation of this displayed fiber bundle.

edges.label: Thalamocortical arm
edges.description: The thalamic relationship supplies broader circuit context. Intermediate basal-ganglia relays are omitted; this drawing is not a complete closed loop.

steps.title: Locate the cortical entry point
steps.body: Carmi’s H7 deep-TMS protocol targeted medial prefrontal/anterior cingulate circuitry and paired treatment with individualized symptom provocation.
steps.takeaway: Target, coil, and treatment context belong together.
steps.note: A medial cortical approximation is shown, not an H7 field or isolated direct ACC stimulation.

steps.title: Reveal the deep partners
steps.body: The rationale involves frontal–striatal–thalamic circuitry. These deep partners help explain the choice of cortical territory even though the coil is outside the skull.
steps.takeaway: Deep circuitry is relevant without assuming the coil directly stimulates every deep node.
steps.note: Only two circuit arms are shown. Pallidal relays and a complete synaptic loop are omitted.

steps.title: Separate the rationale from the trial result
steps.body: The randomized trial reported more OCD responders with active than sham treatment. This supports the tested protocol; it does not determine which individual tract carried the benefit.
steps.takeaway: Clinical efficacy and a proposed circuit mechanism are different claims.
steps.locator: Results; 38.1% versus 11.1% post-treatment response among assessed participants
steps.note: Reference bundles are shown; no trial-specific stimulated fibers are available.

steps.title: Distinguish neighboring cortical approaches
steps.body: Pre-SMA and dmPFC approaches use different targets and protocols. They should be taught separately from the H7 medial-prefrontal/ACC approach. Open the pre-SMA lesson to follow its STN connection.
steps.takeaway: Neighboring medial frontal labels are not interchangeable.
steps.note: Left hemisphere is isolated to show the medial surface; it does not imply unilateral H7 treatment.

quiz.question: Does this diagram prove that the H7 coil directly stimulates the striatum or thalamus?
quiz.answer: No. Those structures explain the network rationale. The clinical trial did not map selective deep-tract activation.

lessons.title: Pre-SMA and the control of actions
lessons.question: Why connect pre-SMA to the STN?

edges.label: Striatal connection
edges.description: Anatomical work places pre-SMA in associative striatal circuitry. The superior corticostriatal bundle is broad reference anatomy.

edges.label: STN-linked targeting
edges.description: Ji selected a right pre-SMA TMS site using individual STN functional connectivity. The separate 3D hyperdirect-pathway estimate is population anatomy, not the study’s targeting map.

steps.title: Start at pre-SMA
steps.body: Pre-SMA is a medial frontal action-control region, posterior to the dmPFC approach. Ji’s OCD trial stimulated an individually selected right pre-SMA site.
steps.takeaway: The superficial target and deep connectivity reference have different roles.
steps.note: An anterior-SMA anatomical estimate is shown, not Ji’s individual target.

steps.title: Add striatum and STN
steps.body: Pre-SMA participates in striatal and subthalamic circuitry. The striatal arm and the STN-linked targeting relationship are distinct connections, shown with different line styles.
steps.takeaway: The superior corticostriatal tract does not terminate in the STN.
steps.note: The pre-SMA–STN 3D subset is an anatomical estimate with asymmetric source coverage.

steps.title: Understand the targeting experiment
steps.body: In a randomized study of 37 people, Ji used STN connectivity to choose the cortical target. Active treatment improved OCD symptoms more than sham, with associated changes in the functional target network.
steps.takeaway: Connectivity helped choose where to stimulate; the STN was not directly stimulated by TMS.
steps.locator: Abstract; Results; clinical and connectivity analyses
steps.note: One small trial does not establish this pathway as the universal mediator of OCD TMS.

steps.title: Keep the evidence proportional
steps.body: Pre-SMA studies differ in laterality and targeting. Mantovani used bilateral stimulation; Fitzsimmons used left pre-SMA in a different protocol. The right-sided example here belongs specifically to Ji.
steps.takeaway: Always attach a side and protocol to the target name.
steps.note: The right-side display follows Ji’s target; it is not a claim of right-hemisphere superiority.

quiz.question: Is the STN the TMS treatment site in Ji’s study?
quiz.answer: No. Right pre-SMA is stimulated. STN functional connectivity was used to choose that cortical site.

lessons.title: Different entry points, different networks
lessons.question: Why does the DBS location matter?

edges.label: VC-connected network
edges.description: Effective ventral-capsule stimulation volumes were linked predominantly with medial OFC in Tyagi’s tractography analysis.

edges.label: amSTN-connected network
edges.description: Tractography associated the effective amSTN site with lateral OFC, dACC and DLPFC. The diagram omits dACC to keep this comparison compact.

edges.label: Prefrontal connection
edges.description: DLPFC was among the cortical destinations from the effective amSTN stimulation volume. Reference STN pathways are not those individual treatment fibers.

steps.title: Locate the white-matter corridor
steps.body: Capsular DBS places contacts near multiple fiber populations. The ventral capsule and neighboring ventral striatum are close together, so the broad target label alone does not specify the stimulated network.
steps.takeaway: Ask which fibers are near the active contact.
steps.note: The whole internal capsule provides orientation. It does not delineate vALIC or a stimulation volume.

steps.title: Follow the ventral-capsule network
steps.body: In Tyagi’s six-person comparison, effective ventral-capsule stimulation connected predominantly with medial OFC. VC stimulation had a stronger mood effect than amSTN stimulation.
steps.takeaway: A deep white-matter entry point can access distant cortex.
steps.note: General capsular bundles provide context; the study-specific medial OFC pathway is not reconstructed.

steps.title: Compare the subthalamic entry point
steps.body: The amSTN-connected network included lateral OFC, dACC and DLPFC. Both DBS sites reduced OCD symptoms; improved cognitive flexibility was found with amSTN stimulation.
steps.takeaway: Clinical dimensions and connected networks can differ across DBS sites.
steps.locator: Results: Tractography and cognitive flexibility; Figure 3
steps.note: The whole STN and population pathways are shown; the precise amSTN treatment volume is unavailable.

steps.title: Zoom from target names to contacts
steps.body: Tyagi reported the most effective contacts at the dorsal end of the VC/VS lead and the deepest end of the amSTN lead. The contact comparison shows a separate published example of different acute experiences at adjacent contacts.
steps.takeaway: An acute mood change and a long-term treatment response are separate observations.
steps.locator: Tyagi Results: active contacts; Tsai Results/Table 2
steps.note: No “contact 4” rule is inferred. Contact numbering and implanted trajectories vary.

quiz.question: Can the name “VC/VS” alone tell you which cortical network a contact engages?
quiz.answer: No. Location, trajectory and stimulation settings matter. A study’s tractography can support a network interpretation, but the target name is not enough.

lessons.title: A meeting point for mood-related pathways
lessons.question: Why target SCC white matter?

edges.label: Forceps minor / uncinate
edges.description: SCC responder tractography included medial frontal connections through forceps minor and uncinate. These are two distinct fiber systems.

edges.label: Cingulum
edges.description: Cingulum pathways connect the SCC region with rostral and dorsal cingulate territories.

edges.label: Descending connections
edges.description: Subcortical connections were part of responder tractography. The displayed corticostriatal bundle is contextual, not a complete reconstruction of the study’s descending paths.

steps.title: Distinguish cortex from white matter
steps.body: SCC DBS targets white matter beside the subgenual cingulate cortex. The nearby sgACC helps orient us, but a cortical surface is not the DBS stimulation site.
steps.takeaway: The pink surface marks neighboring cortex.
steps.note: The precise SCC white-matter target has no boundary mask in this atlas.

steps.title: Reveal the converging fiber systems
steps.body: Riva-Posse’s work associated response with pathways toward medial frontal, cingulate and subcortical destinations. Prospective targeting sought convergence of four fiber systems: forceps minor, uncinate, cingulum and frontostriatal fibers.
steps.takeaway: The connection pattern may be more informative than a coordinate alone.
steps.note: Reference bundles are shown. Their visual overlap does not define a validated stimulation sweet spot.

steps.title: Understand the evidence for targeting
steps.body: A prospective open-label cohort used tractography to guide targeting. Its encouraging outcomes support further study of this approach, while the absence of a sham comparison limits causal interpretation.
steps.takeaway: Targeting evidence and controlled efficacy evidence answer different questions.
steps.note: The 3D anatomy does not reproduce the cohort’s electrodes or activation volumes.

steps.title: Include the controlled result
steps.body: The larger Holtzheimer sham-controlled SCC trial did not find a significant active-versus-sham benefit during the blinded phase. A compelling circuit model does not erase that result.
steps.takeaway: Teach SCC DBS as an investigational approach with mixed clinical evidence.
steps.locator: Holtzheimer abstract: primary blinded comparison; Riva-Posse cohort
steps.note: The left medial view is for visibility; these DBS studies used bilateral implantation.

quiz.question: Does the pink sgACC surface show the exact SCC DBS stimulation volume?
quiz.answer: No. It locates neighboring gray matter. The DBS target is adjacent white matter, and the patient-specific stimulation volume is not loaded.

dlpfc.label: DLPFC
dlpfc.description: A cortical entry point used in depression TMS. Its functional connections help explain why target location within this broad region matters.

sgacc.label: sgACC
sgacc.description: A deep medial cortical region implicated in mood circuitry. It is a connectivity reference in this TMS lesson; the coil is over the DLPFC.

caudate.label: Caudate
caudate.description: A striatal partner of prefrontal cortex. A healthy-volunteer TMS–PET experiment demonstrated a downstream dopamine response here; it did not test antidepressant efficacy.

mpfc.label: mPFC / ACC
mpfc.description: The cortical territory targeted by the H7 OCD protocol. These broad anatomical regions do not outline the coil’s electric field.

striatum.label: Striatum
striatum.description: Deep nuclei within frontal–basal ganglia circuits. Their inclusion explains the network rationale; it does not mean deep TMS directly stimulates them.

thalamus.label: Thalamus
thalamus.description: A deep partner in cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical circuitry. The diagram shows selected relationships, not a complete synaptic loop.

presma.label: Pre-SMA
presma.description: Medial frontal cortex involved in action control. It lies posterior to the dmPFC approach and is a distinct OCD TMS research target.

stn.label: STN
stn.description: A small deep nucleus involved in action control. Ji used STN functional connectivity to choose a superficial pre-SMA TMS site; the STN itself was not the coil target.

capsule.label: Ventral capsule
capsule.expanded: Ventral anterior limb of the internal capsule
capsule.description: A white-matter corridor containing several fiber populations. A contact’s location within this corridor matters more than the broad target name alone.

mofc.label: Medial OFC
mofc.description: A cortical destination associated with effective ventral-capsule stimulation in Tyagi’s tractography analysis.

amstn.label: amSTN
amstn.description: The OCD DBS target in the anterior-medial STN region. The 3D atlas shows the whole STN as orientation anatomy, not this precise subdivision.

lofc.label: Lateral OFC
lofc.description: A cortical destination associated with effective amSTN stimulation in Tyagi’s tractography analysis.

dacc.label: dACC
dacc.description: A cingulate region included in the amSTN-connected network. Its whole parcel is an anatomical approximation.

scc.label: SCC white matter
scc.description: The depression DBS target is white matter near the subgenual cingulate. The pink 3D surface is neighboring sgACC gray matter; it does not outline the stimulation site.

medial.label: Medial frontal cortex
medial.description: A cortical destination in SCC responder tractography, reached through fiber systems that include forceps minor and uncinate fasciculus.

cingulate.label: Cingulate cortex
cingulate.description: A cortical destination linked to SCC stimulation through the cingulum. The available 3D parcel provides partial cortical context.

subcortical.label: Subcortical destinations
subcortical.expanded: Ventral striatal and other deep destinations
subcortical.description: SCC responder tractography included several deep destinations. Nucleus accumbens supplies one available landmark; it does not represent every destination.

seg_dlpfc.label: L DLPFC
seg_dlpfc.description: The cortical entry point. Seguin modeled each recorded stimulation location using a 10-mm-radius gray-matter sphere. The broad atlas surface is not that individual sphere.

seg_sfg.label: R dorsal SFG
seg_sfg.description: An intermediate region in the cortical route and early-crossing thalamic route. The whole superior-frontal parcel gives orientation; it does not delineate Lausanne parcels 20 and 36.

seg_acc.label: R anterior cingulate
seg_acc.description: An intermediate region in the proposed cortical route. The study labels it right caudal anterior cingulate 1 and relates the route to area 32. The atlas parcel is broader.

seg_lthal.label: L thalamus
seg_lthal.description: A proposed relay before the interhemispheric crossing. The connectome uses a whole-thalamus parcel; it does not resolve individual thalamic nuclei.

seg_rthal.label: R thalamus
seg_rthal.description: A proposed relay after the early interhemispheric crossing. This is a modeled network step, not a measured evoked response.

seg_lmed.label: L medial SFG
seg_lmed.description: A medial frontal intermediate region, labeled left superior frontal 14 in the study. The atlas provides a broad medial-frontal estimate rather than that exact parcel.

seg_rmed.label: R medial SFG
seg_rmed.description: A medial frontal intermediate region, labeled right superior frontal 7 in the study. It is distinct from the more dorsal SFG node in the schematic.

seg_sgc.label: R sgACC
seg_sgc.description: The downstream reference: a 10-mm-radius gray-matter sphere centered at MNI (6, 16, −10). Seguin calls this SGC. The atlas shows neighboring sgACC anatomy, not the study sphere.

contactCase.title: One lead, different immediate experiences
contactCase.setting: Reported test: 6 V · 210 μs · 130 Hz · monopolar
contactCase.description: Compare adjacent contacts 1 and 2. Both elicited smiling/laughter, but reported euphoria differed. These are observations in one person, not a prediction for another patient.

contacts.title: Deepest contact
contacts.detail: At 6 V, the report describes smile/laughter with euphoria. Smell and chest tightness were also reported.
contacts.locator: Results: Psychiatric responses; Table 2, case 1, contact 0

contacts.title: Second from the tip
contacts.detail: At 6 V, smile/laughter was accompanied by reported euphoria. The table also lists smell, chest tightness and increased sexual drive at this voltage.
contacts.locator: Results: Psychiatric responses; Table 2, case 1, contact 1

contacts.title: Third from the tip
contacts.detail: At 6 V, smile/laughter occurred without reported euphoria. Smell, chest tightness and increased sexual drive were also listed at this voltage.

contacts.detail: Table 2 lists no smile/laughter response for this contact across the tested voltages. Smell was reported at 6 V. The text does not supply an exact euphoria rating for this contact at 6 V.

contactCase.limits: The lead drawing preserves nominal contact dimensions. It is not implanted into the atlas: the study does not supply a matched patient tractogram or a validated tract assignment for these individual responses. No activation volume is estimated.
contactCase.takeaway: A smile, a subjective mood change, and sustained improvement in OCD are different outcomes. Nearby contacts can differ, and the contact number alone is not an anatomical label.

machadoCase.frame: Millimeters relative to the posterior-inferior margin of the anterior commissure (AC); axes aligned to the AC–PC line.

lead.name: Modified 3387 INS
lead.exception: One participant had a standard 3387 on the left, with 3-mm center spacing.

clusters.name: Ventral striatal region

effects.right: Dizziness, anxiety, alertness and energy were frequent (2–3 participants).
effects.left: Warmth was consistent; dizziness, anxiety and flushing were frequent.

clusters.interpretation: Several nearby structures may contribute: ventral striatum/pallidum, anterior commissure, fornix and ventral capsular fibers. This study could not isolate their contributions.

clusters.name: Ventral capsule above the AC

effects.right: Energy, alertness, laughter, dizziness and talking were frequent.
effects.left: Energy, alertness, warmth, calmness and nausea were frequent.

clusters.interpretation: The authors proposed engagement of orbitofrontal-connected ventral capsular fibers and associated loops. This is an anatomical explanation, not a measured tract-specific cause.

clusters.name: Middle portion of the ALIC

effects.right: Dizziness, anxiety, calmness, reduced mood and fatigue were frequent.
effects.left: No consistent or frequent effects. Warmth, energy, dizziness and calmness were isolated.

clusters.interpretation: The response pattern differed from the ventral clusters. Absence of a reported category is not a prediction of no effect in another patient.

machadoCase.limits: Each point is an average across retained contacts from several people. It is not one person’s electrode. CC3 was too dispersed for response clustering. These coordinates have not been registered into the atlas.
machadoCase.conclusion: Acute mood changes varied with location and side. The paper did not establish that an immediate mood lift predicts sustained antidepressant benefit.
